Looking at this problem, I need to count arrangements of 5 Red, 5 Blue, and 5 Green containers in a line where every container has at least one same-colored neighbor.

**Key Observation:** Every container must have a same-colored neighbor, so every maximal block (run) of same-colored containers must have size ≥ 2. A block of size 1 would be an isolated container with no same-colored neighbor — forbidden.

**Block structures for each color:** For 5 containers of one color, the compositions into parts ≥ 2 are:
- (5) — one block of size 5
- (3,2) — two blocks, sizes 3 and 2 (left to right)
- (2,3) — two blocks, sizes 2 and 3 (left to right)

No 3-block composition exists since 2+2+2 = 6 > 5. So each color has either 1 or 2 blocks.

**All blocks are distinguishable:** Blocks of different colors are distinguishable. Blocks of the same color always have different sizes (only (2,3) or (3,2) possible), so they are distinguishable too.

**Counting strategy:** For each choice of block counts $(n_R, n_B, n_G) \in \{1,2\}^3$, count permutations of all distinguishable blocks with no two same-colored blocks adjacent (inclusion-exclusion on "bad adjacency" events for each color's block-pair).

---

**Case 1: (1,1,1) — all colors have 1 block.** $N=3$ blocks: R(5), B(5), G(5), all different colors.
$$3! = 6$$

**Case 2: (2,1,1) — one color has 2 blocks.** $N=4$. Choose which color: 3 ways. Blocks: X(2), X(3), Y(5), Z(5). Constraint: X(2), X(3) not adjacent.
$$\text{Valid} = 4! - 2\cdot 3! = 24 - 12 = 12$$
$$\text{Total} = 3 \times 12 = 36$$

**Case 3: (2,2,1) — two colors have 2 blocks.** $N=5$. Choose which color has 1 block: 3 ways. Blocks: X(2), X(3), Y(2), Y(3), Z(5). Two bad-adjacency events $A$ (X-pair adjacent), $B$ (Y-pair adjacent).
$$|A| = 2\cdot 4! = 48,\quad |B| = 48,\quad |A\cap B| = 2\cdot 2\cdot 3! = 12$$
$$\text{Valid} = 120 - 48 - 48 + 12 = 36$$
$$\text{Total} = 3 \times 36 = 108$$

**Case 4: (2,2,2) — all colors have 2 blocks.** $N=6$. Blocks: R(2), R(3), B(2), B(3), G(2), G(3). Three bad-adjacency events $A_R, A_B, A_G$.
$$|A_i| = 2\cdot 5! = 240, \quad |A_i \cap A_j| = 2^2 \cdot 4! = 96, \quad |A_R \cap A_B \cap A_G| = 2^3 \cdot 3! = 48$$
$$|A_R \cup A_B \cup A_G| = 3(240) - 3(96) + 48 = 720 - 288 + 48 = 480$$
$$\text{Valid} = 720 - 480 = 240$$

---

**Grand Total:**
$$6 + 36 + 108 + 240 = \boxed{390}$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
